Lifestyle and behavior recommendations f.Explanation: Smoking cessation is crucial for improving overall health and reducing the risk of second cancers and comorbidities. This recommendation is supported by the retrieved context emphasizing the importance of quitting smoking to reduce lung cancer risk and other health issues.

Achieving and maintaining a healthy weight can reduce the risk of comorbidities, improve prognosis, and enhance quality of life. This is particularly important for cancer survivors to avoid recurrence and manage symptoms.

Regular physical activity, including at least 150 minutes of moderate or 75 minutes of vigorous aerobic exercise per week, along with strength training exercises at least 2 days per week, can improve prognosis, reduce cancer-related symptoms, and enhance overall health.

A dietary pattern high in vegetables, fruits, whole grains, and legumes, low in saturated fats, and limited in alcohol consumption is recommended to reduce the risk of all-cause mortality and improve overall health.
Limiting alcohol intake to no more than one drink per day can reduce the risk of cancer recurrence and improve overall health outcomes.
Regular follow-up care for non-cancer conditions and general health concerns is essential for managing comorbidities and maintaining overall health.
